claims.claim: Regulation II still requires every US debit card to be enabled on at least two unaffiliated networks, the structural basis for the PIN-debit networks' merchant routing business through 2026.
claims.quote: prohibits all issuers and networks from restricting the number of networks over which debit transactions may be processed to less than two unaffiliated networks
claims.title: Regulation II (Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page undated; it lists rule milestones of 2011-06-29, 2012-07-27, 2022-10-03 and 2023-10-25.

claims.claim: Regulation II bars issuers and networks from inhibiting merchants' routing choice over any enabled network, which governs how STAR, Accel, NYCE, SHAZAM and peers compete for volume.
claims.quote: inhibiting a merchant's ability to direct the routing of a debit transaction over any network that the issuer has enabled
claims.title: Regulation II (Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The Fed's October 25, 2023 proposal to lower the large-issuer debit interchange cap was still listed as the latest Regulation II action on the Board's page as of 2026-09-25, with no final rule shown.
claims.quote: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on a proposal to lower the maximum interchange fee that a large debit card issuer can receive
claims.title: Regulation II (Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Predates the Sept 2024 window; included because the page shows no later pricing action, an absence finding for the timeline.
